why: H0 unchanged at 62/15/1/22: the 2026 shock was absorbed by official holders' own cash and Treasury sales with no dollar funding break, and markets price little Fed capture, which offsets a Hormuz closure priced as a coin flip into 2028.
H1 S1 45 to 44: the stablecoin bid for bills proved cyclical, flat at about $304B for a year while the Fed added $370B of bills (R3A).

H1 S2 22 to 23: official holders raised 2026 crisis dollars by selling $254B of Treasuries and crisis lines for non-core states are moving to conditional Treasury deals, a small push toward neutral reserves (R3A accepted in half, because no new gold data backs the link).

H2 S1 32 to 31 and S4 30 to 31: income and payroll taxes carry 86.2% of federal receipts while the labor share sits at a record low 52.8% and watt or compute taxes would raise under 1%, a slow erosion of the base behind Treasuries (R3B).
